name: Stylized 3D
traits: sculpted characters with pushed proportions: big heads and hands, tapered limbs
soft painted materials instead of real skin, cloth or metal
strong readable silhouettes and repeated shape language
warm key, cool rim, coloured soft shadows
bestFor: mascots with a lot of acting
warm comedy with one clear emotional turn
suits: household, food and personal-care products with simple rigid shapes; friendly, optimistic brands
stylePara: Stylized 3D animation: characters are sculpted with deliberately exaggerated proportions, oversized heads and hands, tapered limbs and simplified chunky noses, and every surface reads as a soft painted material rather than real skin, fabric or metal; forms are rounded and designed, with clear silhouettes; light is a warm key with a cool rim and gentle coloured bounce, shadows soft and tinted; textures are simplified, with faint brush-like detail painted into the colour; sets are simplified to match the characters and repeat their shapes; nothing aims at photographic realism.

rendering.line: no outlines: forms read through sculpted volume, rim light and silhouette
rendering.shading: soft diffuse shading with gentle subsurface warmth on skin, tinted (not grey) shadows, a small soft specular only on eyes and the product
rendering.colour: saturated but harmonised palette with warm skin and cool shadows; product colours exact
rendering.texture: simplified painted textures, faint brush strokes, no pores, fibres only suggested
rendering.lighting: three-point film lighting: warm key, cool rim, coloured bounce from the set

motion: Keyed pose-to-pose acting with clear arcs: anticipation before each action, overshoot and settle, squash and stretch on bodies but never on the product; key poses held 6-12 frames so the acting reads; full motion on ones at 24 fps, with snappy timing rather than floaty capture-like drift.
camera: Virtual camera that behaves like a real lens: 35-50 mm for acting, 85 mm for close-ups with shallow depth of field, slow dolly or short crane moves; one move per shot, no spinning orbits.
avoid: heads shrinking back to realistic proportions mid-shot
fake lettering on packaging and shop signs
sheets: Each character sheet is a turnaround (front, three-quarter, side, back) on neutral grey plus one row of three expressions (neutral, worried, delighted); the sheet prompt states the head-to-body ratio (e.g. head about one third of body height); the product is rendered in the same soft painted shading but with its exact shape and label colours, best from a Blender render as the first reference.
risk: Seedance normalises the exaggeration: over 8 s heads shrink, hands turn realistic and faces drift from the sheet between shots. Send the turnaround as the STRICT IDENTITY reference in every shot, repeat the proportion in STYLE and the CAST RULE, and keep the product a rigid prop that never squashes.

example.prompt: Stylized 3D animated still: a sculpted woman in her thirties with an oversized head, a big round dark bun and a soft orange top holds a small green glass bottle with a yellow cap in both large hands, standing in a simplified sunny kitchen whose rounded cupboards echo her shapes; beside her a droopy fern with chunky leaves sags on the windowsill; warm key light through the window, cool rim on her shoulder, tinted soft shadows, painted materials, no realistic skin. Vertical 9:16. No text.
